record.original_question: For a skew Boolean algebra S, study two relaxations of the definition: first, drop normality while requiring only that S is symmetric, has 0, and has S/D a Boolean lattice; second, drop symmetricity while requiring only that S is normal, has 0, and has S/D a Boolean lattice. For each resulting generalization, determine its structure, whether it forms a variety, and how it is related to skew Boolean algebras.

evidence.quote: Study objects obtained by relaxations of the definition of an SBA S.
What if normality is dropped and one requires only S is symmetric, has 0 and S/D is a Boolean lattice?
What if symmetricity is dropped and one requires only S is normal, has 0 and S/D is a Boolean lattice?
Do they form a variety (in each case)? How are they related to SBAs?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A skew lattice is an algebra (S; ∧, ∨) of type (2,2) in which both ∧ and ∨ are associative and idempotent and satisfy the absorption identities x ∧ (x ∨ y) = x = x ∨ (x ∧ y) and (x ∧ y) ∨ y = y = (x ∨ y) ∧ y. On any skew lattice, Green's relation D is defined by x D y iff x ∧ y ∧ x = x and y ∧ x ∧ y = y (equivalently x ∨ y ∨ x = x and y ∨ x ∨ y = y); the quotient S/D is the maximal lattice image of S. A skew lattice S is called:
• symmetric if for all a, b ∈ S, a ∧ b = b ∧ a iff a ∨ b = b ∨ a;
• normal if x ∧ y ∧ z ∧ w = x ∧ z ∧ y ∧ w holds identically;
• with 0 if there is an absorbing element 0 such that 0 ∧ x = x ∧ 0 = 0 and 0 ∨ x = x ∨ 0 = x.

A skew Boolean algebra (SBA) is a symmetric, normal, distributive skew lattice with 0 such that S/D is a Boolean lattice, equipped additionally with a relative complement operation \ making the fibers over S/D Boolean.

Problem. Consider the following two relaxations of the SBA axioms:
(A) Drop normality: study algebras S that are symmetric, possess 0, and whose maximal lattice image S/D is a Boolean lattice, but are not required to be normal.
(B) Drop symmetricity: study algebras S that are normal, possess 0, and whose maximal lattice image S/D is a Boolean lattice, but are not required to be symmetric.

For each of the two classes (A) and (B):
1. Describe the structure of its members (e.g., a decomposition or representation theorem analogous to known results for SBAs).
2. Determine whether the class forms a variety (i.e., is definable by identities in a suitable signature, possibly including a complement-like operation or 0).
3. Describe precisely how the class is related to the variety of skew Boolean algebras (inclusions, reflective/coreflective subcategories, identities that must be added to recover SBAs, etc.).
artifact.status_search_result: A search for work on relaxations of skew Boolean algebras dropping normality or symmetricity (while retaining 0 and a Boolean S/D) did not turn up a definitive structural/varietal classification of these two specific generalizations. Related results on skew Boolean algebras, skew Heyting algebras, and discriminator varieties exist, but no source verifies that the two proposed relaxations have been characterized as varieties or related explicitly to SBAs.

status_evidence.snippet: A skew lattice is symmetric if a∨b=b∨a iff a∧b=b∧a. Normal means x∧y∧z∧w=x∧z∧y∧w.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the standard definitions of symmetric and normal skew lattices used in the problem.

status_evidence.title: Free skew Boolean algebras (arXiv:1510.07539)
status_evidence.snippet: Skew Boolean algebras form a variety.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms SBAs themselves form a variety; the status of the two relaxations remains unaddressed in accessible sources.

status_evidence.title: On skew Heyting algebras (arXiv:1410.8780)
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizations of skew Boolean structures dropping certain axioms have been considered but a structural classification of the specific relaxations above is not given.
status_evidence.claim: No found source resolves the two specific relaxations posed.
